forces.title: Irish hotel capital investment shifts towards enhancing existing assets
forces.description: Capital investment in Irish hotel real estate is increasingly prioritizing refurbishment, repositioning, energy efficiency, and guest experience upgrades. This structural shift by investors and operators away from speculative new-build expansion influences future supply dynamics and asset quality focus within the specialized hotel property market.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Phased withdrawal of state-contracted hotel accommodation improves supply
forces.description: The Irish government's phased withdrawal of State-contracted commercial accommodation by March 2027 is a policy-linked factor that will gradually improve tourism accommodation availability. This release of stock, while positive for destination capacity, is not expected to immediately or uniformly dilute pricing power for hotel real estate asset owners.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

forces.title: Energy price volatility and supply chain costs pressure healthcare real estate margins
forces.description: The Irish healthcare sector, particularly energy-intensive residential and hospital care settings, is exposed to sustained energy price volatility. Higher fuel, utility, and imported medical equipment costs feed directly into operating expenses for property owners. Limited ability to pass through these rising costs creates significant margin pressure.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Public investment in health infrastructure drives sector development for asset owners
forces.description: Public capital investment, with approximately €9.25 billion committed under Ireland's National Development Plan (2026–2030) for health infrastructure, is a key driver for sector development. This funding, focused on areas like surgical hubs and community care, shapes private capital deployment in healthcare real estate.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

forces.title: Dutch senior housing construction lags government targets and demand
forces.description: Construction of senior housing in the Netherlands is significantly lagging government targets, with only 11% of the annual goal met in 2024. This shortfall, driven by factors like higher construction costs and lack of municipal targets, exacerbates the supply-demand mismatch despite growing demand from an aging population for specialized senior real estate.
forces.source_title: Mix of incentives and pressure is needed to unlock senior housing market in…

forces.title: Higher construction costs and absent municipal targets hinder senior housing supply
forces.description: The development of senior housing in the Netherlands is hampered by relatively higher construction costs due to accessibility requirements, and the absence of quantitative building targets in municipal housing programs. This makes building regular homes more attractive for developers and investors, exacerbating the supply deficit in specialized senior real estate.
forces.source_title: Mix of incentives and pressure is needed to unlock senior housing market in…

forces.title: Policy incentives and targets could unlock Dutch senior housing market potential
forces.description: Activating the Dutch senior housing market requires a mix of incentives and pressure, including promoting benefits, reducing moving barriers, making subsidy schemes accessible to developers and investors, and setting explicit municipal targets for senior homes. These measures could stimulate both demand and supply for this specialized real estate segment.
forces.source_title: Mix of incentives and pressure is needed to unlock senior housing market in…

forces.title: Robust hotel transaction activity signals strong investor confidence in Ireland
forces.description: Ireland's hotel sector saw record-breaking transaction activity in 2025, estimated at €1.7 billion, including significant acquisitions by private groups and the government. This indicates strong investor confidence and liquidity in hotel real estate assets, supporting valuations and future development prospects, despite government winding down some accommodation contracts.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hospitality Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

forces.title: European healthcare real estate market sees increasing consolidation and M&A
forces.description: The European healthcare real estate sector is undergoing significant consolidation, with examples like Aedifica's merger with Cofinimmo and PHP's acquisition of Assura. This trend, along with British Land's acquisition of Life Science REIT, indicates a focus on income-anchored platforms and asset quality, signaling a strategic shift for property owners in this specialized segment.
forces.source_title: European real estate now has real momentum as liquidity and sentiment improve

forces.title: Irish hotel owners prioritize existing asset upgrades over new construction
forces.description: Irish hotel real estate owners are increasingly prioritizing refurbishments, repositioning, and product enhancement, focusing on asset life extension and energy efficiency. This trend, expected to dominate capital investment decisions in 2026, implies a more subdued pipeline for new hotel construction, especially outside Dublin.
forces.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Hospitality Sector H2 2025 Insights and H1 2026 Outlook

viewpoints.title: Irish hotel real estate investment prioritizes existing asset enhancement over new builds
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland observes that capital investment in Irish hotel real estate is prioritizing refurbishment, repositioning, energy efficiency, and guest experience upgrades over speculative new-build expansion. Investors and operators are focusing on improving existing assets, driven by a need for operational efficiency and value creation, while supply from state-contracted accommodation is expected to gradually return.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish hotel market outlook cautiously positive, forecasting stable occupancy and RevPAR growth
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland presents a cautiously positive H2 2026 outlook for the Dublin hotel market, forecasting stable occupancy at 83.8% and modest RevPAR growth of 1.1%. Stronger RevPAR momentum is noted in some regional markets. The gradual withdrawal of state-contracted accommodation should enhance tourism availability without immediately impacting pricing power for hotel real estate owners.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Hospitality Sector H1 2026 Insights and H2 2026 Outlook July 2026

viewpoints.title: Irish healthcare real estate investment focuses on improving existing facilities, not new builds
viewpoints.description: Bank of Ireland reports that capital investment in the Irish health sector is primarily directed towards improving existing facilities through refurbishment, energy efficiency upgrades, and administrative digitalization, rather than new build expansion. This trend is influenced by rising construction costs, planning constraints, and a generally more cautious investment environment for healthcare property owners.
viewpoints.source_title: Bank of Ireland Sectors Team — Developments & Insights May 2026

viewpoints.title: Dutch senior housing market growth sluggish, requiring incentives for demand and supply
viewpoints.description: ING Think highlights that the Dutch senior housing market is expanding slowly, facing both demand-side reluctance from older adults to move and supply-side constraints. Despite an aging population and government targets for 290,000 senior homes by 2030, construction in 2024 met only 11% of its annual goal, indicating a significant mismatch requiring policy intervention.
viewpoints.source_title: Mix of incentives and pressure is needed to unlock senior housing market in…

viewpoints.title: European real estate sector recovering, with healthcare a key investment focus
viewpoints.description: ING Think indicates a cautiously improving European real estate market in 2026, with the healthcare sector identified as having significant scope for larger investments and transactions. Acquirers are observed prioritizing income-anchored platforms and cash flow-producing assets, as evidenced by recent M&A activities involving major healthcare REITs, suggesting strong strategic interest in this specialized segment.
viewpoints.source_title: European real estate now has real momentum as liquidity and sentiment improve
